blocks.content: The Constitution of India is neither completely rigid nor completely flexible. It provides a well-defined procedure for amendment so that the Constitution can evolve with changing political, social and economic conditions. The power and procedure of constitutional amendment are given under Article 368 in Part XX of the Constitution.
1. Meaning of Constitutional Amendment

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 368 in Part XX of the Constitution grants Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and specifies the procedure.
A Constitutional Amendment Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament, but cannot be introduced in state legislatures.
Amendments affecting federal provisions require ratification by at least half of the state legislatures by a simple majority.
The President must give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill; assent was made mandatory by the 24th Amendment Act, 1971.
Parliament cannot alter or destroy the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution as laid down by the Supreme Court in 1973.

blocks.content: • A constitutional amendment refers to a change, addition, or modification in the provisions of the Constitution.
• It allows the Constitution to adapt to new needs and challenges.
• The power to amend the Constitution lies with the Parliament of India.
2. Constitutional Provision (Article 368)
Article 368 provides the procedure for amending the Constitution. It states that Parliament has the power to amend any part of the Constitution according to the specified procedure.
3. Types of Constitutional Amendments

cells: More than 50% of members present and voting
Creation of new states, change in boundaries
Majority of total membership + 2/3 members present and voting
Special majority in Parliament + approval by half of State Legislatures

blocks.content: 4. Procedure of Amendment
• The amendment bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
• It must be passed by the required majority in both Houses.
Article 368 of the Constitution deals with the powers of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
• In certain cases, approval by at least half of the State Legislatures is required.
• After approval, the bill is presented to the President.
• The President must give assent; he cannot withhold assent.
5. Matters Requiring State Ratification
• Election of the President.
• Distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States.
• Representation of States in Parliament.

rows: Majority of members present and voting in each House
2/3rd members present & voting + absolute majority of total membership in each House
2/3rd members present & voting + absolute majority of total membership in each House
Ratification by simple majority in at least 50% of state legislatures

blocks.content: • Judiciary structure such as Supreme Court and High Courts.
6. Important Constitutional Amendments

cells: Added Ninth Schedule and restrictions on certain Fundamental Rights
Called the Mini Constitution; added Fundamental Duties
Removed Right to Property from Fundamental Rights

blocks.content: 7. Basic Structure Doctrine
• The Basic Structure Doctrine was established by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).
• It states that Parliament cannot amend the basic structure of the Constitution.
• Examples of basic structure elements include supremacy of the Constitution, rule of law, judicial review, federalism, and secularism.
8. Significance of Constitutional Amendments
• Helps the Constitution remain relevant over time.
• Allows democratic changes through legal procedures.

items: Prior recommendation/permission of the President is NOT required to introduce a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
There is NO provision for holding a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament in case of a deadlock over a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
State legislatures cannot initiate any bill or proposal for constitutional amendment.
The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) is commonly referred to as the 'Mini-Constitution' due to its vast changes.

blocks.content: • Maintains balance between rigidity and flexibility.
EXAM Important Facts
• Article 368 deals with constitutional amendments.
• 42nd Amendment is known as the Mini Constitution.
• Basic Structure Doctrine was established in 1973.
• Right to Education was introduced by the 86th Amendment.
